subject: Biotechnology
title: Biodiesel and Algal Fuels
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Biodiesel and Algal Fuels.

hook.text: Algae produce 30 times more oil per hectare than soybeans — microscopic green factories could fuel the future.

buildup.text: Biodiesel converts vegetable oils or algal lipids into fatty acid methyl esters — a drop-in replacement for diesel fuel.

discovery.text: Algae grow in wastewater, seawater, or even CO2-enriched air — no farmland, no fresh water, no food competition.

twist.text: Algal biofuels have been technically feasible for decades — but cost $5 to $10 per gallon, far above fossil fuel prices.

climax.text: Synthetic biology engineers algae with higher lipid content and faster growth — pushing costs toward economic viability.

punchline.text: Tiny algae, enormous potential — algal biofuels await their economic breakthrough.

quiz.question: Why haven't algal biofuels replaced fossil fuels despite their technical advantages?
options: Algae cannot produce enough oil for large-scale use
Production costs of $5-10 per gallon remain far above fossil fuel prices
Algal oil cannot be converted into standard diesel fuel
